info.title: Watcher API
info.description: Trajectory ingestion, grading, and query API for Watcher. Concepts and integration guides: https://watcher-docs.apolloresearch.ai

get.description:
Return the deployment's public auth configuration.

Unauthenticated by design: clients (analyzer SPA, watcher CLI/hooks)
call this to discover the auth mode and, in WorkOS mode, the client id
to start a sign-in with, so the value is configured once server-side
instead of being baked into each client.

post.description:
Report whether the current credential has every requested permission.

Unknown and ungranted permission slugs have identical semantics: both are
returned in ``missing``. The endpoint evaluates effective authority, so
administrators and server-side service identities satisfy the same checks
as they do on the protected API operation itself.
Exchange a WorkOS authorization code for access + refresh tokens.

Start a device-authorization sign-in (RFC 8628) for a headless client.

Unauthenticated by design — it produces credentials. Proxies WorkOS's
device-authorization endpoint so clients need nothing but this server's
URL; the WorkOS client id stays server-side configuration.

Poll the outcome of a device-authorization sign-in.

While the user hasn't finished approving, answers 400 with
``detail.code`` ``authorization_pending`` (keep polling) or ``slow_down``
(poll less often); a dead attempt answers 400 with ``access_denied`` or
``expired_token``. On success this runs the same org resolution as
``/callback`` and returns both tokens in the body — the caller is a CLI
with its own credential store, so there is no cookie to hide the refresh
token in.

Refresh an expired access token.

The refresh token is read from the httpOnly cookie (set by /callback) or from
the request body for server-side callers that store it and send it explicitly
(e.g. Watcher proxy, scripts).

Sign out the user — revokes the WorkOS session and clears the refresh cookie.

Reads the ``sid`` (session ID) from the JWT in the Authorization header
and calls WorkOS to revoke the session server-side. This ensures the user
must fully re-authenticate on next sign-in (no auto-complete from a cached
WorkOS session).

schema.title: Response Auth Logout V1 Auth Logout Post

get.description:
Return the current authenticated user's profile.

Includes display identity (user_id, email, role), org context
(organization_id, organization_name, memberships for multi-org
callers), and effective permission slugs after organization policy;
known Watcher permissions granted by built-in roles are included in
both WorkOS and proxy modes. The role is for display only: clients gate
controls on permissions, matching the backend authorization policy.
Return current organization settings.

patch.description:
Update organization settings.

Fields omitted from the body are left unchanged; fields sent as null are
cleared. Null is only accepted for clearable fields; null on any other
field returns 400. The Slack webhook URL is encrypted at rest on deployments
with encryption configured (Watcher Cloud is) and stored as supplied
otherwise. It is clearable via null, unless the deployment supplies it
through `SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL`, in which case any body mentioning
`slack_webhook_url` is refused whole with a 409.

get.description: Return the org's current managed settings document for this path.

put.description:
Validate and save a new version of the org's managed settings document.

The document is validated against the Watcher settings schema (merged onto
the builtin defaults, exactly as machines will apply it); an invalid
document returns 422 with the field and value errors and stores nothing.
This endpoint is also the programmatic write path: an org API key with the
write permission can call it from CI.

get.description: Return the JSON Schema of the managed settings document, for editor hints.

schema.title: Response Get Org Managed Settings Schema V1 Organization Managed Settings  Path  Schema Get

get.description:
Return the document machines should apply for this path, or 404 when unmanaged.

Any authenticated member of the org can read this (machines authenticate
with per-user credentials, so a member JWT need not carry the admin-only
settings permission). An org or user API key is the exception: it must carry
org:settings:read, the same slug the other settings routes enforce. 404
covers both "the org distributes via MDM" and "no document saved yet";
clients treat it as "no managed settings" and keep their last-known-good
file. That expected 404 carries a structured detail
(``{"code": "no_managed_settings", "message": ...}``) so clients can tell
it apart from a routing-layer 404, whose body is a plain string.

Return which graders the org's current settings document activates, by stage.

The Monitors page uses this to show whether a monitor (a grader) is rolled
out. It is only meaningful when the org distributes via Watcher: under MDM
the stored document is not what machines run, so ``monitors`` is empty and
the caller shows the MDM state instead. Machines apply the document merged
onto the builtin defaults, so a grader set only by those defaults still
counts as rolled out.
Simple health check. Always returns healthy if the process is running.
Return the build stamped into this deployment ("dev" when unstamped).

post.description:
Ingest one or more trajectories. Returns leaf hashes and session ID.

User attribution: signed-in users write their own sessions. Service keys
carrying ``sessions:write:any`` may honor ``identity.login_name`` for
proxy-capture (Tailscale Aperture) attribution; keys carrying only
``sessions:ingest`` write unattributed sessions.

A Claude Code session id or Codex thread id names one session per
organization. An upload attributed to a user (a signed-in user's, or one
attributed through ``identity.login_name``) joins that session when it has
no owner and makes the user its owner. When another user owns it, the
request is rejected with 409 ``session_owner_conflict``: that trajectory
is not stored, earlier trajectories in the request stay stored, and later
ones are not processed. An upload attributed to no user joins the session
whoever owns it and leaves the owner unchanged.

409.description: The upload names a Claude Code or Codex conversation whose session another user owns (code session_owner_conflict)

post.description:
Append a delta of transcript entries to an existing session's chain.

``trajectory_id`` names the anchor: the last message the client
successfully uploaded. The delta continues the chain after it, producing
rows identical to a full re-upload of the whole transcript. Clients fall
back to POST /v1/ingest on any 404 or 409 from this route.

Service keys carrying ``sessions:write:any`` may append across owners;
those carrying only ``sessions:ingest`` may append only to unattributed
sessions.

Persist decisions for already-ingested tool calls, alerting on newly flagged ones.

This endpoint is intentionally batch-oriented and post-ingest-only. The
transcript must already exist in Watcher so each decision can be resolved to
a canonical session message. Decisions that cannot be resolved to an
ingested tool call, or that reference missing/already-linked grade IDs, are
reported in the response and skipped. Other valid decisions in the same
batch are still persisted.

Slack alerts for flagged tool calls fire from here (not from grading): only
once the decision is uploaded are the coding agent (from the session) and the
Analyzer deep link available. Alerts fire once per decision — only for
decisions newly inserted by this call, so re-pushes (e.g. pending ->
resolved) do not re-notify.

Grade trajectories with explicitly named graders.

Callers may grade their own stored sessions. Grading another user's stored
session requires ``sessions:grade:any`` and access to that session's content.
Results respect findings permissions. Grading supplied messages needs no
session-read grant; attaching tool-call results to a session requires write
authority. Flagged-grade Slack notifications are sent after the response,
only for DB-backed trajectory grading. Tool-call grading
(``tool_call_run_kind``) persists the grade but does NOT notify here — its
alert fires later, at decision ingest (``POST
/v1/tool-call-decisions/batch``), once the coding agent and Analyzer link
are known. Plain ephemeral grading never notifies.

499.description: Client disconnected while ephemeral grading was in flight

post.description:
Evaluate one or several pending calls, or accept a transcript with no pending call.

Scalar input returns one decision or an HTTP refusal. A batch returns an
ordered result per input; a refused input carries status_code/detail while
other inputs continue. Null or empty input returns an empty list and only
ingests the top-level `messages`. All inputs share one transcript, recorded
once along with successful judgments.
Decisions attach to each input's `tool_use_id`. For evaluated requests,
`ephemeral` skips transcript, decision, and grade persistence while retaining
usage accounting. Enforce and observe both return completed judgments,
including when ephemeral or the caller cannot record sessions.

An append cannot be ephemeral and requires authority to write its parent
session. It returns a HookAppendResponse containing the committed next
anchor and an ordered results list, even for scalar or transcript-only
input. Messages and available decisions are stored before success; reuse
the returned anchor directly for the next append. Recording failure is
HTTP 503 and can follow committed messages. Its body retains ordered
`results`, including denies, without an `append_after` cursor. Apply those
decisions and retry the same append to finish recording.

`settings_overrides` accepts YAML text or a JSON object and uses the normal
administrator permission rules. An override that changes a locked setting
is refused with HTTP 422; one that repeats it is accepted. The effective `enforcement.mode` selects enforcement, observation,
or ingestion only. Observe returns the completed judgment with a deferred
applied decision. Paused and unnamed calls do not evaluate; authorized
callers still record the transcript. HTTP 422 errors use a list of detail
entries, including validation and settings overrides.

The caller enforces returned decisions; this endpoint does not execute or
block tools itself. Deterministic stages precede triage and gateway grading.
`mode=triage_only` bounds grading depth, while `skip_rules` and
`policy_version` support clients that already evaluated deterministic stages.
Stage waits are bounded in both enforce and observe, but detached grades
can finish and count usage after a timeout or disconnect.
Callers own transport-failure handling.

Completed evaluations are reused per org, session and tool-use ID when the
stored name and JSON arguments match. Current enforcement posture is applied
to the original judgment; policy or grading-depth changes do not invalidate
it. `force_regrade=true` evaluates again and permits replacing the recorded
decision, including with an observation. Failed and unjudged evaluations
retry normally. Reuse requires known external IDs, ingestion authority and
permission to read the resolved session; id-less, ephemeral and write-only
callers evaluate normally, as do unknown stored call metadata shapes.
Reuse creates no new grades, usage or alerts, though the transcript still
ingests. Concurrent misses and retries before post-response recording may
evaluate more than once. Paused mode never evaluates, even when forced.

With `format="raw"`, send a provider request (`request_body`) and its
complete response (`response_body`) in one supported wire format (OpenAI
Chat Completions or Responses, Anthropic Messages, Gemini generateContent
or Bedrock Converse) plus the client-facing endpoint path in `url`, instead
of `messages` and `input`. Watcher converts the pair and evaluates the
selected new client calls. The response is a list, one output per selected
call in response order; each `tool_use_id` is the provider's call ID.
Gemini calls get generated IDs and are matched by order within the selected
candidate. `response_index` selects by zero-based array position and is
required when there are multiple alternatives. Deliver only the selected
choice or candidate. Match every
executable client call to exactly one output before applying its decision.
Withhold the response if a call has no output, IDs are duplicated, or an
output cannot be matched to a call. For Gemini, require equal call and output
counts. An error output is not permission to execute a call.

Anthropic calls before the final `fallback` block have no output. An empty
list means no client calls were selected, not that the original response
contains none. There is no limit on the number of tool calls in one response.
Known coding harnesses are recognized from the request and `user_agent` and
contribute their session IDs. Their own helper requests without selected
client calls (Claude Code background requests, Codex thread titles,
approval reviews and memory extraction, Antigravity titles) return `[]`
and are not recorded. The gateway still checks those responses for
executable calls.

404.description: The append session or anchor is missing or outside the caller's write scope

409.description: The append cannot continue this anchor (detail.code: anchor_conflict)

413.description: The request body exceeds the endpoint's size limit

503.description: Append messages committed but decision recording failed (detail.code: append_recording_failed). The body retains ordered results, including denies, but no append_after cursor.

post.description:
Accept a supported coding-agent request/response capture from Tailscale Aperture for asynchronous monitoring.

Configure Aperture with events=["entire_request"] and
send=["request_body", "response_body"]. The API key must have
sessions:write:any so metadata.login_name can attribute the session.
Admin enforcement.mode selects observation or ingestion only (paused);
this asynchronous transport always caps enforcement at observe. Only tool
calls in the response are evaluated. Text-only turns are ingested too.

A 202 confirms admission, not completed grading or durable storage.
Unsupported formats and malformed provider bodies are logged after the
ACK. Captures require recognized coding-harness identity, using the
per-format markers documented in the hooks reference. Other applications
are skipped.

403.description: The caller cannot attribute sessions to the webhook's developer

413.description: The webhook exceeds the hook request size limit

503.description: The bounded delivery workers are full; this delivery was not accepted

get.description:
List the server-managed monitors, with their client-facing facts.

Requires only authentication (any org member): the response carries no
org data and no monitor internals — name, description, context policy, and
token budget only, never the prompt or model.

post.description:
Grade with the monitor serving ``role`` — no grader UUID, model, or prompt client-side.

Ephemeral ``messages`` grades persist as tool-call audit rows under the
role's run kind (``policy_triage``/``policy_gateway``) and return a
``tool_call_grade_id`` per result, exactly like a UUID-addressed tool-call
grade. DB-backed grading (``trajectory_ids`` + ``session_id``) requires
ownership or ``sessions:grade:any``; content access is not required to run
a server-managed monitor. Results respect findings and content permissions. Supplied-message
grades require session write authority when attached to a session.
Both modes enforce grading caps and usage allowances.

Responses omit ``model``: which model a monitor runs is a server-side
policy choice, not part of the client contract.

499.description: Client disconnected while ephemeral grading was in flight

get.description:
Return the org's monitor customization (empty instructions when never set).

This is the whole customization surface an admin sees for the monitors:
their own text plus each monitor's description (from GET /v1/monitors).

put.description:
Set the org's monitor customization (an empty instructions string clears it).

The instructions are injected into every monitor's prompt inside a
delimited org-policy section, so they are validated here for the length cap
and for the reserved delimiter sequences the injection fence cannot safely
carry; an invalid document returns 422 and stores nothing. Overwrites in
place — customization history is deliberately not retained (grade
reproducibility is out of scope), and the write is audit-logged without
content.

get.description:
List all sessions with pagination and sort. For filtered queries use POST /sessions/search.

Callers without ``sessions:findings:read:any`` see only their own sessions
(naming another user in ``user_id`` returns 403).

post.description:
Search sessions with filtering, pagination, and sort. Same read-scope rules as GET /sessions.

Sessions with no recorded messages never match, whatever the filters.

get.description:
Return organization-wide aggregate session metrics, optionally filtered by owner.

Requires ``sessions:aggregates:read:any`` through a role or credential grant,
including when filtering to the caller's own ``user_id``. Otherwise returns HTTP 403.
List category filter options from the score definitions of session-visible graders.
Get full session detail including trajectories and grades. 404 for sessions the caller can't read.

delete.description: Scrub one organization-scoped session, or return 404 when it is not visible to the caller.

get.description: List all trajectories in a session. 404 for sessions the caller can't read.

Read one tool call's decision and full grader outputs with findings access.

Ownership or ``sessions:findings:read:any`` is required. Raw tool arguments
and grading-input messages are always empty; their content is available only
through transcript reads. ``has_result`` reports only whether a response was
recorded for the call. Returns 404 for inaccessible, missing, or scrubbed
sessions and missing decisions. ``tool_use_id`` is a query parameter because
transcript-local IDs can contain characters such as slashes and ``#``.

Get trajectory content through ownership, ``sessions:content:read:any``, or an active session content approval.

Return 404 when content is inaccessible or scrubbed. Session grades and
tool-call decisions are included only with findings access; session summaries
remain available with content access alone.

The ``view`` parameter picks the payload shape and defaults to ``truncated``,
which caps tool outputs and user pastes and stubs out ``data`` content blocks,
leaving marker fields (``content_truncated``, ``content_original_chars``) so
clients can offer a full fetch. Callers that need storage-faithful message
content must explicitly request ``extended``.

The literal trajectory id ``latest`` resolves server-side to the session's
most recent trajectory (the response carries the resolved id), so
session-scoped links can load a transcript in a single request. 404 when
the session has no trajectories.

Returns at most one grade: the most recent non-errored grade recorded
anywhere on the requested trajectory's hash chain (a grade is stored
against the trajectory hash current when it ran, so earlier grades sit on
prefix hashes). A trajectory whose chain was never graded falls back to
the session's most recent grade, so a graded session never presents as
ungraded; errored grades are returned only when nothing else exists.

Extended-thinking signatures (opaque replay payloads inside reasoning content
blocks) are omitted from message content to keep responses small; the readable
reasoning text is unaffected.

Get one message's full stored content by its ``message_ref``.

Backs per-elision expansion: the truncated trajectory view marks what it
elided and carries each message's ``message_ref``; this endpoint returns
that single message with full content, so expanding one item never
refetches (or renders) the whole trajectory. There is no ``view`` param —
the truncated form is what the trajectory response already provides.
Extended-thinking replay payloads are stripped like every other read path.

Requires ownership, ``sessions:content:read:any``, or an active session content
approval. Returns 404 for inaccessible or scrubbed content and for refs not in the session.

post.description:
Queue a deep review of the session's latest transcript, or return the one already queued.

Requires ownership or ``sessions:grade:any``, without requiring content access.
Repeating the request for an unchanged transcript returns the same operation.
If that review failed, a fresh attempt is queued. 402 when the organization
is over its monthly grading cap.

409.description: The session has nothing to review, or a review cannot be started for it

get.description: Return the deep-review work to show when opening the session; 404 if the session is not visible.
Poll one on-demand deep review; 404 if it is not this session's review or the session is not visible.

post.description:
Search tool calls with filtering, pagination, and sort.

Read scope matches the sessions list exactly: a caller holding
``sessions:findings:read:any`` sees the whole organization and may filter by any owner,
while everyone else is confined to their own calls and naming somebody else is
refused rather than silently answered about themselves.

Only calls Watcher recorded a decision about are listed, which is the same
population the dashboard's tool-call counts are computed over.

get.description: Return the allowed models and frontend suggestions from the registry.
List latest non-archived version of each grader visible to the authenticated org.

post.description: Create a new grader (version 0) owned by the current organization and user.

get.description: Get a specific grader version, even if archived (for grade provenance lookups).
Get the latest non-archived version of a grader owned by the org or built-in.

patch.description: Create a new grader version with the given updates. Only the creator may modify.

delete.description: Archive all versions of a grader (soft delete). Only the creator may delete.

post.description: Search graders by name and header/footer content. Scoped to the authenticated org + built-in.

get.description:
Return grading usage aggregates: a by-date series plus per-user/model/grader window totals.

The date window is capped at 180 days: wider explicit ranges are rejected
with 422, and an omitted ``start_date`` defaults to 180 days before
``end_date`` (or now).

parameters.name: start_date

schema.description: Window start; defaults to 180 days before end_date.
schema.title: Start Date

parameters.description: Window start; defaults to 180 days before end_date.

get.description:
Return whether grading is currently capped for the caller's org, and the call figures behind it.

Readable by any org member — no permission gate — since it backs the
grading-paused alert on member-visible pages and carries nothing sensitive.

Runs the same check the grade routes run, so the readout cannot drift from
what blocks — including its 500 when the counter cannot be read, rather than
reporting a cap status we could not verify.
Return the current authenticated user's profile.

get.summary: List My Session Content Access Requests
get.description:
List only the signed-in user's access requests in their current organization.

Admins also receive only their own requests. No session-read permission is
required. Service credentials without a user identity receive HTTP 401.
Results are newest first; status filters use the stored review decision,
so approved requests include those whose ``valid_until`` has passed.
``active_only`` limits results to pending requests and currently valid approvals.

post.summary: Create My Session Content Access Request
post.description:
Request content access to a known session in the caller's organization.

Returns the existing request on repeated submissions while pending. No
findings grant is required. Missing, foreign, or scrubbed sessions return
404; already-readable content returns 409. Credentials must identify a user.

get.description:
List members of the caller's organization.

Requires ``users:read:any``; rows include ``email`` since that same
permission gates reading other users' emails.

Get a user by id, scoped to the current org's membership.

Returns the caller's own row, or any org member if the caller has
``users:read:any``. Otherwise 404 — we don't leak the existence of
cross-user rows through error codes.

List requests from all users in the current organization, newest first.

Requires ``sessions:access-requests:review``, included in the admin role.
Repeat ``status`` to include multiple decisions. Approved results include
expired approvals. ``view`` selects pending requests, active approvals, or
historical (denied, revoked or expired) requests using database time. Filters combine;
pending/active counts always cover the organization. Identities are included, never content.

patch.summary: Review Session Content Access Request Endpoint
patch.description:
Approve or deny a pending request, including your own.

Requires ``sessions:access-requests:review`` and a signed-in user identity.
Approval lasts eight hours unless a shorter, timezone-aware ``valid_until``
is supplied. Expiries must be in the future and at most eight hours after
review (422). A completed decision cannot be changed (409). Missing or
foreign requests return 404; scrubbed content cannot be approved (409).

post.summary: Revoke Session Content Access Request Endpoint
post.description:
Revoke an active approval, preserving its original review and expiry.

Requires ``sessions:access-requests:review`` and a signed-in user identity.
Missing or foreign requests return 404. Pending, denied, expired, or already
revoked requests return 409. The server records the revoker and revocation time.

ActivatedMonitor.title: ActivatedMonitor
ActivatedMonitor.description:
One monitor selected by the current Watcher Live settings document, and how.

`grader_id` is the resolved identity: a custom grader ID or a managed monitor
ID from GET /v1/monitors when a stage uses its shipped default. A managed ID
is not the settings value selecting that role and is not listed by GET
/v1/graders. `stages` lists the selected live-pipeline stages; a monitor can
fill more than one. `enforced` is true only when
every one of those bindings is locked against local override on machines.

ActivatedMonitorsResponse.title: ActivatedMonitorsResponse
ActivatedMonitorsResponse.description:
Response for GET /v1/organization/managed-settings/{path}/monitors.

A read-only projection of which custom or managed monitors the current
document activates. Consumed by the Analyzer's Monitors and Managed
Settings pages. Managed identities describe current-client routing, not
observed fleet activity.

`monitors` is populated only when the org distributes via Watcher: under MDM
the stored document is not what runs on machines, so rollout cannot be
asserted and the list is empty. `distribution` is included so the response is
self-interpreting (an empty list means "nothing activated" under `watcher`
but "not applicable" under `mdm`). `version` is the document version the list
was computed from (0 when none saved).

AdminSessionContentAccessRequest.title: AdminSessionContentAccessRequest
AdminSessionContentAccessRequest.description: An organization request with its requester, reviewer, and revoker identities.

pending_count.title: Pending Count
pending_count.description: Pending requests in the organization, independent of list filters.

active_count.title: Active Count
active_count.description: Currently valid approvals in the organization, independent of list filters.

AdminSessionContentAccessRequestListResp.title: AdminSessionContentAccessRequestListResponse
AdminSessionContentAccessRequestListResp.description: A page of organization requests, ordered newest first.

ApertureHookAccepted.title: ApertureHookAccepted
ApertureHookAccepted.description: Admission acknowledgement; processing finishes asynchronously and is not durable.

ApertureHookMetadata.title: ApertureHookMetadata
ApertureHookMetadata.description:
Tailscale Aperture-owned identity fields; unknown additions are accepted.

``request_id`` identifies a capture, never a conversation. ``session_id``
is Aperture's own session id: one it took from the client (prefix
``xsid_`` or ``pisn_``) is recorded as the conversation id of a capture
without a native one, and any other value is ignored. The provider key
and URL describe routing and do not identify the developer's harness.
``user_agent`` supplies application evidence to the format parser. The
parser applies the supported harness's marker and system-identity rules;
selecting a wire format alone never admits an application. These fields
classify captured traffic; they do not authenticate the caller.

ApertureHookRequest.title: ApertureHookRequest
ApertureHookRequest.description:
The fixed webhook envelope with both required send types enabled.

Raw request and reconstructed response objects are forwarded to the selected
format parser. A null or absent response represents an upstream call that
produced no response body and is skipped: Aperture omits ``response_body``
when the client disconnects before the provider answers (capture status 0).
Extra metadata and send types are ignored.

ApertureLog.title: ApertureLog
ApertureLog.description: A whole-file Tailscale Aperture proxy capture, referenced by its object storage location.

AppliedDecision.title: AppliedDecision
AppliedDecision.description:
What Watcher actually did about a tool call.

``DEFERRED`` means Watcher deliberately stood aside (grading skipped by a
snooze/ignore bypass or admin pause, or a judgment observe mode withheld)
and the host agent's own permission flow gated the call. ``NOT_EVALUATED``
means the call was never routed through Watcher at all (e.g. Codex tools
that bypass the PermissionRequest hook). Watcher live's local ``block``
outcome folds into ``deny`` at upload — what Watcher *did* is deny — while
the block flavor is preserved on the local row's judged value.

AuthClientConfig.title: AuthClientConfig
AuthClientConfig.description:
Response from GET /v1/auth/client-config.

Public (unauthenticated) deployment auth descriptor: lets browser SPAs
and CLI/hook clients discover how to authenticate against this server
from nothing but its URL. ``workos_client_id`` is non-None only in
WorkOS auth mode. Client IDs are public by construction (they appear
in every authorize URL), so exposing one here leaks nothing.

AuthUser.title: AuthUser
AuthUser.description:
The signed-in user's identity as sign-in endpoints report it.

``id`` is the WorkOS user id; ``user_id`` is Watcher's own user id, present
once the sign-in has created or matched the Watcher user (it can be absent
only when WorkOS reported no email to match by).

can_read_findings.title: Can Read Findings
can_read_findings.description: Whether this caller may read this session's findings.

can_read_content.title: Can Read Content
can_read_content.description: Whether this caller may read this session's content. Scrubbed messages remain unavailable.

agent_platform.title: Agent Platform
agent_platform.description: Reported coding agent. Retained SDK adapter identities can name the agent, including for historical sessions stored as 'other'. Reporting does not change the stored ingestion identity. Clients must tolerate additional platform strings.

sources.title: Sources
sources.description: Distinct canonical ingestion sources among retained session messages, sorted; same values as ``SessionSummary.sources``. Empty for a scrubbed session, whose messages are gone.

AvailableSessionDetailResponse.title: AvailableSessionDetailResponse
AvailableSessionDetailResponse.description: Session detail whose trajectory content remains available.

applied_decision.description: Original permission action, independent of grading success.

judged_decision.description: Original policy judgment, including a failure-policy fallback.

enforcement_mode.description: Mode in which the original permission action was recorded.

tool_use_id.title: Tool Use Id
tool_use_id.description: Transcript-local identifier of the tool call.

message_ref.title: Message Ref
message_ref.description: Reference of the message containing the tool call.

tool_input_preview.title: Tool Input Preview
tool_input_preview.description: Raw tool-argument preview; null without content access to the session.

decision_summary.title: Decision Summary
decision_summary.description: Concise title or context from the policy grade that supplied severity_score, falling back to the recorded decision summary.

AvailableToolCallListItem.title: AvailableToolCallListItem
AvailableToolCallListItem.description: A tool-call row whose transcript evidence remains available.

BypassReason.title: BypassReason
BypassReason.description:
Developer/repo-scoped grading bypass active at decision time.

``SNOOZE`` is a time-boxed developer pause of grading, started from the menu
bar. ``WATCHER_IGNORE`` means the session's working directory matched a
``.watcher-ignore`` marker file (note the hyphen in the file name; the enum
value uses an underscore), so grading is skipped for that repo; it is
admin-gated by the ``watcher_ignore_files`` policy. Either one makes Watcher
stand aside, so the call is applied as ``deferred``.

Orthogonal to ``EnforcementMode``: a snooze started in enforce mode keeps
suppressing grading after an admin switches the machine to observe, and both
facts are recorded. NULL when no bypass window was active.

ClaudeAPIMessage.title: ClaudeAPIMessage
ClaudeAPIMessage.description: A message from the Claude API. Accepts extra fields like 'type', 'stop_reason'.

ClaudeCodeAttachment.title: ClaudeCodeAttachment
ClaudeCodeAttachment.description:
Payload of an ``attachment``-type JSONL entry.

Attachments carry out-of-band context injected into the conversation (hook
output, task reminders, diagnostics, ...). Almost all of them are telemetry,
with one exception that matters for ingestion: ``type == "queued_command"``
records the delivery of a message the human typed while the agent was
mid-turn. Queued messages are written to the JSONL *only* as this attachment
(plus a ``queue-operation`` enqueue record) — there is no corresponding
``user`` entry — so the human's words live exclusively in ``prompt``.

``prompt`` is a plain string for text-only messages, or a list of content
blocks when the queued message included images. Empirically no other
attachment type carries a ``prompt``.

ClaudeCodeEntry.title: ClaudeCodeEntry
ClaudeCodeEntry.description:
One entry from a Claude Code JSONL file.

The JSONL contains many types: user, assistant, file-history-snapshot,
progress, system, summary, attachment. We accept all types and filter to
conversation-carrying entries (user/assistant with messages, plus
queued-command attachments) during chain building.

append_after.description: Append messages after this exact stored session/trajectory anchor. The server loads its prefix before validating or grading calls. Requires session-write authority and cannot be combined with ephemeral. Successful append responses return the committed next anchor and ordered results. Retry once with the full transcript and without append_after on 404, 409, or 422.

external_ids.title: External Ids
external_ids.description: Distinct conversation IDs from the harness and gateway, keyed by source. Required unless ephemeral is true; send every id you have, e.g. {"claude_code": "<Claude Code session uuid>", "other": "<your own conversation id>"}. The keys also name the harness. A caller with no id at all records id-less by sending an explicit null value, e.g. {"other": null} or {"claude_code": null}: the session is then found by transcript prefix. With append_after the explicit anchor selects the session; any non-null external IDs must already belong to that session.

force_regrade.title: Force Regrade
force_regrade.description: Evaluate again even when this session and tool-use ID have a completed judgment. The new result may replace the recorded decision, including in observe mode. Otherwise a readable completed judgment with matching tool arguments is reused, regardless of policy version, under the current enforcement posture.

settings_overrides.title: Settings Overrides
settings_overrides.description: Per-request settings as YAML or a JSON object; at most 65,536 characters of YAML or serialized JSON. Administrator permission locks apply.

messages.description: The Claude Code session file as JSONL entries (or only those after append_after), in the shape trajectory ingestion accepts.

ClaudeCodeHookRequest.title: ClaudeCodeHookRequest
ClaudeCodeHookRequest.description:
Judge pending calls with a Claude Code session's own JSONL transcript as their context.

``messages`` holds the session file's entries, or only those after
``append_after``. Claude Code's hooks report every call with its
``tool_use_id`` and in the shape the model sent it, so a selected call is
checked against the file's record of that ID when the file holds it, and
judged from the report alone when the agent has not written it yet.

ClaudeCodeTrajectory.title: ClaudeCodeTrajectory
ClaudeCodeTrajectory.description: A trajectory in Claude Code JSONL format (entries from the .jsonl file).

CodexContentItem.title: CodexContentItem
CodexContentItem.description:
One item inside a ``content`` or ``output`` array.

The ``type`` annotation lists the values the parser handles. Unknown
values still parse (they fall through the ``| str`` branch) and are
ignored.

CodexEntry.title: CodexEntry
CodexEntry.description: One line from a Codex session rollout file. ``type`` says which payload fields are set.

CodexGitInfo.title: CodexGitInfo
CodexGitInfo.description: Git info from a session_meta payload. Empty when the cwd isn't a git checkout.

append_after.description: Append messages after this exact stored session/trajectory anchor. The server loads its prefix before validating or grading calls. Requires session-write authority and cannot be combined with ephemeral. Successful append responses return the committed next anchor and ordered results. Retry once with the full transcript and without append_after on 404, 409, or 422.

external_ids.title: External Ids
external_ids.description: Distinct conversation IDs from the harness and gateway, keyed by source. Required unless ephemeral is true; send every id you have, e.g. {"claude_code": "<Claude Code session uuid>", "other": "<your own conversation id>"}. The keys also name the harness. A caller with no id at all records id-less by sending an explicit null value, e.g. {"other": null} or {"claude_code": null}: the session is then found by transcript prefix. With append_after the explicit anchor selects the session; any non-null external IDs must already belong to that session.

force_regrade.title: Force Regrade
force_regrade.description: Evaluate again even when this session and tool-use ID have a completed judgment. The new result may replace the recorded decision, including in observe mode. Otherwise a readable completed judgment with matching tool arguments is reused, regardless of policy version, under the current enforcement posture.

settings_overrides.title: Settings Overrides
settings_overrides.description: Per-request settings as YAML or a JSON object; at most 65,536 characters of YAML or serialized JSON. Administrator permission locks apply.

messages.description: The Codex rollout as JSONL entries (or only those after append_after), in the shape trajectory ingestion accepts.

CodexHookRequest.title: CodexHookRequest
CodexHookRequest.description:
Judge pending calls with a Codex rollout as their context.

``messages`` holds the rollout's entries, or only those after
``append_after``. Codex's hooks report a shell call as ``Bash`` and leave
out how it runs (its working directory, sandbox escalation), so each
selected call must name its ``tool_use_id`` (the rollout's ``call_id``),
and the rollout's record of that call supplies those details. A call
without an ID, or one the rollout does not hold, is never allowed
automatically.

CodexLocalShellAction.title: CodexLocalShellAction
CodexLocalShellAction.description: Action body for a ``local_shell_call``. ``command`` is a list of argv strings, not one string.

CodexPayload.title: CodexPayload
CodexPayload.description:
All payload fields the Codex JSONL parser reads, in one class with every field optional.

Handlers check ``type`` to know which fields are set. The ``type``
annotation lists the values the parser handles; unknown values still parse
(the ``| str`` branch) and are skipped with a logged warning.

Validators normalise a few looser shapes so every field has one type, as
``ClaudeCodeEntry`` does for Claude Code transcripts.

CodexReasoningSummaryItem.title: CodexReasoningSummaryItem
CodexReasoningSummaryItem.description: One item in the ``summary`` array of a ``reasoning`` payload.

CodexTrajectory.title: CodexTrajectory
CodexTrajectory.description: A trajectory in Codex JSONL format (raw events from the session rollout file).

ContentBlock.title: ContentBlock
ContentBlock.description:
A content block from a Claude API message.

Accepts extra fields (e.g. 'signature' on thinking blocks) without failing.

ContentReasoning.title: ContentReasoning
ContentReasoning.description:
Reasoning content.

See the specification for [thinking blocks](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/extended-thinking#understanding-thinking-blocks) for Claude models.

CreateSessionContentAccessRequest.title: CreateSessionContentAccessRequest
CreateSessionContentAccessRequest.description: Request content access to a known session; identity comes from authentication.

DecidedBy.title: DecidedBy
DecidedBy.description:
Who settled a call once Watcher handed it on, as the uploading client recorded it.

``PERSON`` is a person answering a permission prompt: Watcher's own, or the host agent's
native prompt when the agent reported that a person answers it. ``AGENT_REVIEW`` is the
host agent's automated approval reviewer answering its native prompt (Codex's "Approve for
me"), so the call's outcome is in ``tool_status`` and there is no ``human_decision``.
``INTERRUPT`` is the person interrupting the turn before the call was answered, which
leaves the call ``cancelled``. That includes a turn interrupted while Watcher was still
grading, which Watcher records as its own deny.

NULL when the call is still unsettled, when the client cannot tell who answered (a host
that does not say who answers its native prompt), and on rows from clients that predate the
field. Readers then infer the actor from ``human_decision`` and ``tool_status``.

Rely on it only for escalations. Outside them a value can sit beside Watcher's own verdict:
the interrupted-while-grading deny above, and the hook path's pending-response merge, which
keeps a stored value when a later verdict replaces the row's decision.

DecisionSource.title: DecisionSource
DecisionSource.description: Subsystem that produced the policy decision.

DeepReviewRequestResponse.title: DeepReviewRequestResponse
DeepReviewRequestResponse.description:
Queue state of an on-demand deep review, for polling until it finishes.

``queued`` and ``running`` are in progress. ``succeeded`` means the review
finished; its report is published as the session's deep-review grade unless
a newer review already replaced it. ``failed`` means the review gave up after
its retries or was cancelled; send the request again to start a new review
(refused with 409 once this transcript has failed too many times).

DeviceAuthorizationResponse.title: DeviceAuthorizationResponse
DeviceAuthorizationResponse.description:
Response from POST /v1/auth/device/authorize (RFC 8628 device authorization).

Mirrors WorkOS's device-authorization response verbatim: the Watcher API
proxies the call so headless clients need nothing but the server URL — the WorkOS
client id stays server-side configuration. ``device_code`` is the secret
the client polls with and must never be shown to the user; ``user_code``
is the short code the user confirms in a browser on any other device.

DeviceTokenResponse.title: DeviceTokenResponse
DeviceTokenResponse.description:
Response from POST /v1/auth/device/token once the user approved the sign-in.

Unlike ``TokenResponse``, the refresh token travels in the JSON body: the
caller is a CLI with its own on-disk credential store, not a browser, so
there is no cookie jar to hide it in.

DocumentCitation.title: DocumentCitation
DocumentCitation.description: A citation that refers to a page range in a document.

DocumentRange.title: DocumentRange
DocumentRange.description: A range specifying a section of a document.

EnforcementMode.title: EnforcementMode
EnforcementMode.description:
Admin-set, machine-wide enforcement mode snapshot at decision time.

Stamped on every decision — including plain allows — so observe-mode
would-be block rates have a denominator. Absent on decisions uploaded by
older clients that did not send it.

ExternalIdSource.title: ExternalIdSource
ExternalIdSource.description:
Where an external conversation id in a hook request comes from.

Keys of `PreToolUseHookRequest.external_ids`. Each maps onto the external-id
source the matching ingest path already stores, so a hook-recorded decision
converges onto the session Watcher Live (`claude_code`, `codex`) or the
Tailscale Aperture log ingest (`aperture`) created for the same
conversation; `other` is the gateway's own id and matches only other hook
calls.

GatewayResult.title: GatewayResult
GatewayResult.description:
The gateway monitor's verdict on the gated call.

`failure_mode` is the monitor's label for the kind of risk it scored
(its vocabulary is the monitor's own, not an enum of this contract).

GradeRequest.title: GradeRequest
GradeRequest.description:
Request body for POST /v1/grade.

Grades with graders the caller addresses explicitly by UUID. Two payload
modes: ``messages`` (pre-assembled message lists, graded as sent) or
``trajectory_ids`` plus ``session_id`` (stored trajectories). ``grader_ids``
is required:
this endpoint never chooses a grader for the caller. To run the
server-managed monitors without holding grader UUIDs, use
POST /v1/monitors/{role}/grade instead.

``tool_call_run_kind`` records an ephemeral grade as tool-call audit
provenance. When set, each grade result includes a ``tool_call_grade_id``
that can later be attached to a tool-call decision, and the caller may send
``session_id`` + ``tool_use_id`` so the grade row records which call it
graded from birth.

cost_usd.title: Cost Usd
cost_usd.description: Estimated USD cost of this request, including retries with reported usage, at prices set on the server. Null for UUID-addressed grading, missing usage or pricing, or stored-session grading without findings or content read access to that session. Otherwise zero when no model is called. Provider attempts whose usage is hidden by the provider client cannot be included.

GradeResponse.title: GradeResponse
GradeResponse.description:
Results from UUID-addressed or role-addressed grading.

Role grading also reports the cost across every trajectory and retry in
this request. Only the selected role runs: an input triage assessment is
not another billed stage. Stored-session cost requires findings or content
read access to that session. UUID-addressed grading leaves cost unknown.
Older servers omit the field, so clients must accept an absent value.

GradeResult.title: GradeResult
GradeResult.description:
API representation of a trajectory grade.

DB-backed grades include trajectory and session identifiers. Ephemeral
grades omit persisted trajectory identifiers and use ``trajectory_index`` to
identify the trajectory's position in the request.

Stored session summaries (including nested report summaries) require content
access. Mixed read responses omit fields outside the caller's read permissions.

Callers can resolve ``(grader_id, grader_version)`` to the exact grader
configuration used via GET /v1/graders/{grader_id}/{version}.

GraderDetail.title: GraderDetail
GraderDetail.description:
Full grader detail including header, footer, and output configuration flags.

Graders are always self-describing rows: the graders API never serves the
server-managed monitors' identity rows (those surface via /v1/monitors).

GraderSummary.title: GraderSummary
GraderSummary.description:
Grader in list responses (no header/footer).

Graders are always self-describing rows: the graders API never serves the
server-managed monitors' identity rows (those surface via /v1/monitors).

GradingFailure.title: GradingFailure
GradingFailure.description:
Why a graded stage could not decide, when the org's failure policy answered instead.

`code` is the stable vocabulary to branch and alert on — each value calls
for a different remedy (a larger caller budget or `triage_only` for
`timeout`, server capacity for `at_capacity`, a raised allowance for
`allowance_exhausted`, an outage for `grader_failed` and `no_result`).
`message` is human-readable and may change between releases. `stage` is
the graded stage that failed, so a caller that pauses a failing stage
(the Watcher client's gateway breaker) does not blame the gateway for a
triage failure.

GradingUsageBreakdownRow.title: GradingUsageBreakdownRow
GradingUsageBreakdownRow.description:
Usage totals for one breakdown value (a user, model, or grader).

``key`` is the stable identifier (user id, model name, or grader id) and
``label`` the display name (email, model name, or grader name); both are
null for usage that cannot be attributed to the dimension (e.g. live
grades whose decision never linked back to a session). Token-field
semantics match ``GradingUsageBucket``.

GradingUsageBucket.title: GradingUsageBucket
GradingUsageBucket.description:
One time bucket of the grading-usage aggregation.

Request counts split by pipeline: ``trailing_requests`` are turn-review
grades, ``triage_requests``/``gateway_requests`` are the two live
pre-tool grading stages. ``cost`` is the estimated USD spend for the
bucket (excluding unpriced models). Cost and token fields are null when the deployment does not expose raw token
details (see ``GradingUsageResponse.token_details_enabled``); otherwise
they are totals across the bucket. Cache token fields follow the naming of
``GradeUsage``: cache_write is tokens written to the provider prompt
cache, cache_read is tokens served from it.

GradingUsageCostBucket.title: GradingUsageCostBucket
GradingUsageCostBucket.description:
Estimated grading spend (USD) for one time bucket, split by request kind.

Costs are estimated from per-model token rates; usage on models without
configured rates is excluded (see ``GradingUsageResponse.unpriced_models``).
Only present when the deployment exposes token details.

GradingUsageFilterOptions.title: GradingUsageFilterOptions
GradingUsageFilterOptions.description:
Distinct filterable values for the grading-usage view.

``users`` and ``graders`` are org-wide; ``models`` only includes models
with usage inside the requested date window, so the picker never offers a
model that would chart nothing.

GradingUsageGraderOption.title: GradingUsageGraderOption
GradingUsageGraderOption.description: A grader available as a grading-usage filter value.

GradingUsageResponse.title: GradingUsageResponse
GradingUsageResponse.description:
Grading usage aggregates from GET /v1/usage/grading.

``by_date`` holds one row per time bucket, ordered by date ascending;
``by_date_cost`` mirrors it with estimated USD spend per request kind
(empty when token details are hidden), and ``unpriced_models`` lists
models whose usage is excluded from cost estimates for lack of rates.
``by_user``/``by_model``/``by_grader`` hold window totals per breakdown
value, ordered by output tokens descending. ``token_details_enabled``
reports whether this deployment exposes raw token counts; when false, all
token fields are null and only request counts are meaningful.

GradingUsageUserOption.title: GradingUsageUserOption
GradingUsageUserOption.description: A user available as a grading-usage filter value.

HookAppendAnchor.title: HookAppendAnchor
HookAppendAnchor.description:
The exact stored message after which a hook's delta begins.

Obtain the first pair from session search or trajectory ingestion, then use
the committed anchor returned by each successful hook append. An
explicit session and trajectory disambiguate branches; the server never
guesses which leaf the caller observed. A missing anchor returns 404 and
a conflicting continuation returns 409. Retry once with the full transcript
and without this field on 404, 409, or 422 (including older servers).

HookAppendResponse.title: HookAppendResponse
HookAppendResponse.description:
A committed append anchor and its ordered per-call results.

Use ``append_after`` directly in the next append request; it identifies
the last stored message from this request, not a tentative write or a
server-selected latest branch. An empty delta echoes its input anchor.
Messages and available decisions are recorded before this response. Stage
grades that exceeded their wait deadline may still finish afterwards.
``results`` is always a list, including for scalar input, and is empty for
transcript-only ingestion. Another writer can still advance the chain
before the next request, which then uses the normal conflict recovery.

tool_use_id.title: Tool Use Id
tool_use_id.description: Echoes this input's tool_use_id, or null when omitted.

HookCallError.title: HookCallError
HookCallError.description:
A refused input inside a batch; other inputs still receive their own outcomes.

Treat this as the corresponding scalar HTTP error, never as permission to
execute the tool. It carries no judgment and creates no decision record.

HumanDecision.title: HumanDecision
HumanDecision.description: Explicit approval or denial from a human permission dialog.

IngestAppendRequest.title: IngestAppendRequest
IngestAppendRequest.description:
Request body for POST /v1/sessions/{session_id}/trajectories/{trajectory_id}/append.

Appends a delta of raw transcript entries to an existing session's chain.
The session and the anchor (the trajectory_id of the last message the
client successfully uploaded) are named in the path; the server continues
the chain after the anchor, so a session ingested through any mix of full
and append uploads stores rows identical to full-only ingestion. Tailscale
Aperture logs are whole-file proxy captures with no client-side cursor, so
they have no append form.

IngestResponse.title: IngestResponse
IngestResponse.description:
Response from the full ingest and per-session append endpoints.

One shape for both paths keeps client bookkeeping (cursor advance, leaf
tracking) shared. ``trajectory_ids`` echoes an already-stored leaf in two
cases: an append whose delta parsed to zero messages, and a full ingest
that exactly duplicates the caller's own session (which still counts
toward ``duplicate_count``). Either way the client keeps a valid anchor
for its next append.

``ingested_count`` and ``duplicate_count`` are in stored-leaf units, not
uploaded files: a rewound Claude Code file stores one leaf per
conversation branch, so one upload can produce several of either.

``trajectory_ids`` lists the resulting leaves in processing order — for a
rewound Claude Code file, abandoned branches first and the live branch
last, whether each leaf was newly stored or an echoed duplicate. The last
entry is what clients record as their next append anchor, so live-last is
a contract, not a coincidence of storage order.

JudgedDecision.title: JudgedDecision
JudgedDecision.description:
What the decision pipeline concluded about a tool call.

NULL (an absent value) means grading never ran: the call was snoozed,
ignored, admin-paused before any deterministic rule fired, or never routed
through Watcher. A non-null judged value proves the pipeline evaluated the
call, which is what "evaluated" means for dedup ranking and observe-mode
aggregates. The judged and applied values differ exactly when the
enforcement mode withheld enforcement (e.g. an observe-mode would-be deny is
judged ``deny`` with an applied ``deferred``). Watcher live's fail-closed
``block`` outcome folds into ``deny`` on this wire enum.

MessageDetailResponse.title: MessageDetailResponse
MessageDetailResponse.description:
One full-content message from GET /sessions/{sid}/messages/{message_ref}.

Backs per-elision expansion in the Analyzer: the truncated trajectory view marks
what it elided, and this response carries the single message's stored content so
the client never refetches the whole trajectory to expand one item. The message
uses the same wire shape as trajectory-response messages.

ModelTokenBudget.title: ModelTokenBudget
ModelTokenBudget.description:
Token-sizing facts a client needs to fit input to one model family.

``max_input_tokens`` is the model's whole context window and
``max_output_tokens`` its output cap — a client derives its input budget by
subtraction. The tiktoken fields describe how to count: the encoding the
client should tokenize with, and a scaling factor correcting for tokenizers
tiktoken cannot represent.

ModelsConfig.title: ModelsConfig
ModelsConfig.description:
Response shape of ``GET /v1/graders/models``, built from the model catalog.

``suggested`` are catalog entries advertised in the UI; ``enabled`` are the
remaining allowed models (accepted by the free-text input, not advertised
in dropdowns).

context_user_messages.title: Context User Messages
context_user_messages.description: A positive count of recent user messages, or 'all' for the whole transcript.

MonitorContextPolicy.title: MonitorContextPolicy
MonitorContextPolicy.description:
What of the transcript enters a client-invoked monitor's prompt.

Server-owned counterparts of the ``policy_monitors`` client settings: a
client grading by role applies these values instead of its local settings,
so changing what the monitors see becomes a registry edit rather than a
client release. Field semantics match the ``policy_monitors`` section of
the client settings schema.

MonitorCustomizationResponse.title: MonitorCustomizationResponse
MonitorCustomizationResponse.description:
Response for GET/PUT /v1/monitors/customization.

``instructions`` is the org's single custom-instructions text, injected
into every monitor grading for the org; empty string when the org has
never set any (semantically identical to having cleared them).

MonitorInfo.title: MonitorInfo
MonitorInfo.description:
One server-managed monitor as served by GET /v1/monitors.

A monitor's prompt, model, and reasoning are server-owned and not part of
its public description. What a client needs is here: ``context_policy``
says what of the transcript to assemble, and ``token_budget`` carries the
sizing facts for truncation (in place of a model name). Both are null for
the server-invoked roles (``summarize``, ``deep_review``), which assemble
their own context. ``grader_id`` names the row the monitor's grades carry
as provenance.

tool_use_id.title: Tool Use Id
tool_use_id.description: Identifies the pending call for hook requests. Monitor grade linkage uses the request's top-level tool_use_id instead.

MonitoringInput.title: MonitoringInput
MonitoringInput.description:
Structured inputs for monitoring one gated tool call.

The caller sends *what the monitor looks at*; the server owns how it is
formatted into a prompt, so prompt structure can change without a client
release.

The conversation context is ``messages`` — the transcript as structured
``ChatMessage`` objects. The server applies the monitor's served
context policy (user-message window, tool outputs / agent reasoning
withheld) and renders the prompt, so a caller sends its conversation
without reimplementing the calibrated renderer. When both forms are sent
``messages`` wins.

``transcript`` — the same context as pre-rendered per-message text parts,
rendered client-side — is deprecated: current clients send only
``messages`` (a client is never newer than its server), so the form exists
for clients that predate structured messages and is dropped once the
compatibility window moves past them.

``grading_guidelines`` is the watched repository's own guidelines document
(e.g. WATCHER.md), included verbatim as caller-side data.

MonitoringRequest.title: MonitoringRequest
MonitoringRequest.description:
Request body for POST /v1/monitors/{role}/grade.

Names *what* to monitor; the server owns *how*. The monitor in the path
resolves server-side to its prompt, model, reasoning, and context policy,
and the tool-call audit kind derives from the role.

Three mutually exclusive payload modes:

- ``input`` — structured monitoring of one gated tool call: the transcript
  and the call as data, formatted into the monitor prompt server-side.
  The mode clients are expected to use.
- ``messages`` — pre-assembled message lists, graded as sent.
- ``trajectory_ids`` + ``session_id`` — DB-backed grading of stored
  trajectories.

On the two ephemeral modes the caller may also send ``session_id`` +
``tool_use_id`` to identify the gated call being graded (the role's run
kind makes every ephemeral grade here a tool-call audit row).

MonitorsResponse.title: MonitorsResponse
MonitorsResponse.description:
Response for GET /v1/monitors.

Also the monitoring capability signal: a server without server-managed
monitors 404s this path, telling a client to stay on grader-UUID grading.

OrgManagedSettingsDoc.title: OrgManagedSettingsDoc
OrgManagedSettingsDoc.description:
Response for GET/PUT /v1/organization/managed-settings/{path}.

The document is the organization's managed Watcher Live configuration: the
``settings.yaml`` that machines running Watcher Live apply. `yaml` is null
(and `version` 0) when the org has never saved a document for this path. This
response carries only the document; the org-level distribution policy lives
on OrgSettings.

OrgManagedSettingsResolved.title: OrgManagedSettingsResolved
OrgManagedSettingsResolved.description:
Response for GET /v1/organization/managed-settings/{path}/resolved.

The machine-pull view: the Watcher Live document a machine should apply.

expected_version.title: Expected Version
expected_version.description: Version returned by GET; use 0 when no document exists.

OrgManagedSettingsUpdate.title: OrgManagedSettingsUpdate
OrgManagedSettingsUpdate.description:
Request body to save a new version of the org's managed Watcher Live settings document.

Body for PUT /v1/organization/managed-settings/{path}.

slack_alert_detail.title: Slack Alert Detail
slack_alert_detail.description: Slack alert detail level. Findings-only alerts include findings and aggregates, excluding session content.

anyOf.description: Days of session inactivity before stored content is scrubbed.

OrgSettings.title: OrgSettings
OrgSettings.description:
Response from GET /v1/org/settings.

The Slack webhook URL is write-only: responses expose only the
`slack_webhook_configured` flag and `slack_webhook_hint` (the URL's
last 4 characters, for confirming which webhook is set), never the
full URL.

`slack_webhook_managed` is True when the deployment supplies the webhook
URL through the `SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL` environment variable. That value takes
precedence over anything stored per organization, so the configured flag
and hint then describe the deployment's URL, and the settings API refuses
writes to `slack_webhook_url`.

anyOf.description: Days of session inactivity before stored content is scrubbed.

PermissionCheckRequest.title: PermissionCheckRequest
PermissionCheckRequest.description: Permissions the authenticated caller wants Watcher to evaluate.

PermissionCheckResponse.title: PermissionCheckResponse
PermissionCheckResponse.description: Whether the caller has every requested permission and which are missing.

PolicyDecision.title: PolicyDecision
PolicyDecision.description:
Superseded applied-decision vocabulary.

``AppliedDecision`` replaces this enum: it adds ``deferred`` so the server can
tell "Watcher deliberately stood aside" apart from "never routed". This enum
and the ``policy_decision`` field remain so clients and servers on either
side of that change interoperate; new clients should read ``applied_decision``.

append_after.description: Append messages after this exact stored session/trajectory anchor. The server loads its prefix before validating or grading calls. Requires session-write authority and cannot be combined with ephemeral. Successful append responses return the committed next anchor and ordered results. Retry once with the full transcript and without append_after on 404, 409, or 422.

external_ids.title: External Ids
external_ids.description: Distinct conversation IDs from the harness and gateway, keyed by source. Required unless ephemeral is true; send every id you have, e.g. {"claude_code": "<Claude Code session uuid>", "other": "<your own conversation id>"}. The keys also name the harness. A caller with no id at all records id-less by sending an explicit null value, e.g. {"other": null} or {"claude_code": null}: the session is then found by transcript prefix. With append_after the explicit anchor selects the session; any non-null external IDs must already belong to that session.

force_regrade.title: Force Regrade
force_regrade.description: Evaluate again even when this session and tool-use ID have a completed judgment. The new result may replace the recorded decision, including in observe mode. Otherwise a readable completed judgment with matching tool arguments is reused, regardless of policy version, under the current enforcement posture.

settings_overrides.title: Settings Overrides
settings_overrides.description: Per-request settings as YAML or a JSON object; at most 65,536 characters of YAML or serialized JSON. Administrator permission locks apply.

messages.title: Messages
messages.description: Shared conversation transcript, or only new messages when append_after is set. Required for zero or multiple inputs; a scalar or single-item list may supply input.messages instead.

PreToolUseHookRequest.title: PreToolUseHookRequest
PreToolUseHookRequest.description:
Evaluate pending tool calls or ingest a transcript through the generic hook.

Full requests send the conversation in `messages` and select pending calls with
`input`. A scalar input returns one response; a list returns one outcome
per input in the same order, including each input's `tool_use_id`. Null,
omitted, or empty-list input ingests the transcript without grading or
writing decisions and returns an empty list, regardless of enforcement mode.
Named observe calls return completed judgments with a deferred applied
decision. Enforce and observe support ephemeral full requests and evaluation
without session-write permission; recording requires that permission.
All calls share one transcript, which is ingested once when recording is enabled.

Set `append_after` to an explicit session and trajectory ID to send only new messages.
Append requires parent-session write authority and rejects `ephemeral=true`.
The stored prefix loads before validation and grading; pending calls may be in it.
Success returns `HookAppendResponse` with the next anchor and ordered results after recording.
Reuse that anchor directly. HTTP 503 `append_recording_failed` retains ordered `results`
without a new cursor: apply those decisions and retry the same append to finish recording.
On HTTP 404, 409, or 422, retry once with the full transcript and without `append_after`.
Older servers reject the additive field with 422. No implicit latest leaf is chosen.

Input lists accept at most 32 items, including blank or ephemeral inputs.
Larger lists are rejected with HTTP 422 before ingestion or grading.
Batches with multiple inputs require top-level `messages`. Their inputs
must omit `messages` or supply null or an empty list, so the transcript is
sent only once. Scalars and single-item lists may supply `input.messages`;
if both locations are non-null, their transcripts must match. An input
with an explicitly blank tool name only ingests and retains its response shape.
Paused and unnamed inputs need no grading admission;
authorized ingestion still uses normal database resources.

Send structured `messages`, including the assistant message containing each
pending call. Pre-rendered `transcript` and caller `triage_assessment` are
rejected. A recorded named call requires `input.tool_use_id` matching one
call in those messages; different batch inputs must name different ids.
The selected tool name and arguments must match every transcript occurrence
of its ID. Argument object key order is ignored; JSON value types and string
content must agree. Omitted `tool_input` matches an empty arguments object;
explicit null does not. Mismatches return HTTP 422 before grading or ingestion.
`ephemeral` suppresses transcript, decision, and grade persistence, but not
usage. Enforce and observe requests may both use it.

`external_ids` includes each distinct conversation ID from the harness
and gateway, including a separate gateway-issued ID when available.
A null value explicitly opts into transcript-prefix
reconciliation and still names the harness. Recorded requests require this
mapping. `user` supplies the developer email only when the authenticated
caller can impersonate; otherwise attribution stays with that caller.

`settings_overrides` accepts a YAML string or JSON object that the server
will merge onto administrator settings as a local settings layer.
An override that changes an administrator-locked value is refused with
HTTP 422; one that repeats it is accepted. Set `enforcement.mode` there for observe or paused behavior;
omitted overrides inherit the administrator's settings. A gateway's
server-owned capability limit independently prevents unsupported enforcement.

`mode=triage_only` bounds grading depth: triage can allow but cannot deny;
otherwise it escalates without running the gateway monitor. `skip_rules`
is for clients that already evaluated deterministic stages. When they send
`policy_version` (`<version>@<builtin digest>`), a stale token forces those
stages to run again against the server's current policy.

tool_use_id.title: Tool Use Id
tool_use_id.description: Echoes this input's tool_use_id, or null when omitted.

decision.description: The posture-applied verdict to enforce. This endpoint returns allow, deny, escalate or deferred; not_evaluated is never returned — it marks calls that were never routed through Watcher at all.

decision_source.description: The authority that produced the decision. Observe responses retain the deciding stage; bypass means evaluation was skipped, such as for a paused hook.

cost_usd.title: Cost Usd
cost_usd.description: Estimated USD cost of this input's triage and gateway grading, including retries with reported usage. Zero when grading is skipped or reused; null when usage or pricing is missing or a stage is unfinished. Provider attempts whose usage is hidden by the provider client cannot be included.

PreToolUseHookResponse.title: PreToolUseHookResponse
PreToolUseHookResponse.description:
Response body for POST /v1/hooks/pre-tool-use.

`decision` is what the caller should do; `judged_decision` is what the
pipeline concluded before the org's enforcement posture was applied. The
two differ when the posture withholds enforcement. An `observe` response
retains the completed judgment and stage results with `decision=deferred`.
`paused` returns an unjudged `deferred` response and only ingests the transcript.
`escalate` means the call requires human approval before
proceeding — a caller with no human in the loop should treat it per its own
policy (typically block, with `verdict.explanation` as the reason).

`decision_source` says which pipeline stage decided: `threshold`
(terminal per-tool thresholds), `rule` (a command rule; see `rule`),
`bypass` (the effective mode skipped all evaluation), `triage` (the fast monitor
auto-allowed — or, in `triage_only` mode, declined to clear the call),
`policy_gateway` (the authoritative grade), or `grading_error`
(grading failed and the org's failure policy applied; see
`grading_error`). Callers enforce `decision` and alert on
`decision_source`: an `allow` from `grading_error` is the org's
fail-open policy speaking, not a clearance. The thresholds the decision
was judged against are the org's managed settings, not echoed here.

`verdict` is the decision-level view — the score that drove the decision
banded into a label (the gateway's for `policy_gateway`, triage's for
`triage`; null for rule/threshold decisions, which carry no score) plus
the summary and explanation to show. Completed stage results retain their
scores and evidence, including when triage and gateway disagree. A completed
failed grade has no score, but can still carry its persisted grade-row ID.
`tool_call_grade_id` identifies a persisted row attachable to a later decision
upload; ephemeral results have a null ID because no grade row is stored.
A stage that has not completed when its wait expires has no result yet.

PriorHumanDecision.title: PriorHumanDecision
PriorHumanDecision.description:
One recent human-reviewed decision on this session, as data.

``response`` is the human's verdict (e.g. ``allow``/``deny``);
``tool_input`` is the gated call's input as it was stored. The server
renders the list into the monitor prompt's recent-decisions section,
oldest first.

url.title: Url
url.description: Client-facing endpoint path or URL, e.g. /v1/chat/completions.

provider.title: Provider
provider.description: Gateway route or model alias, recorded as provenance.

user_agent.title: User Agent
user_agent.description: The client's User-Agent header, used to recognize harnesses.

response_index.title: Response Index
response_index.description: Zero-based array position of the Chat choice or Gemini candidate; required for multiple alternatives.

RawPreToolUseHookRequest.title: RawPreToolUseHookRequest
RawPreToolUseHookRequest.description:
A pre-tool-use hook request carrying one provider request and its complete response.

``request_body`` is the JSON the client sent to the gateway and
``response_body`` the assembled JSON response the gateway would return,
both in the same wire format: OpenAI Chat Completions or Responses,
Anthropic Messages, Gemini generateContent or Bedrock Converse. Streams must
be assembled into the equivalent non-streaming body first. ``url`` is the
client-facing endpoint path or URL; it breaks ties between formats and is
recorded without credentials, query or fragment.

``external_ids`` carries the gateway's own conversation ID, typically under
``other``. A recognized harness's native ID is added to it; the caller
cannot replace a native ID the harness supplied. With neither, the session
is found by transcript prefix. ``user`` is honored only for callers allowed
to impersonate. The remaining fields have the pre-tool-use hook's meaning.

The response is a list with one output per selected new client call, in
response order. Each ``tool_use_id`` is the provider's own call ID, except
for Gemini, whose calls get stable generated IDs and are matched by order
within the selected candidate. Only the selected choice or candidate may
be delivered. The gateway must match every executable client call it will
deliver to exactly one output before applying its decision. Withhold the
response if a call has no output, IDs are duplicated, or an output cannot
be matched to a call. Gemini requires equal call and output counts.

Anthropic calls before the final ``fallback`` block have no output. An
empty list means no client calls were selected, not that the original
response contains none. There is no limit on the number of tool calls in
one response (the watcher format accepts at most 32 inputs), because a
gateway does not control how many calls a provider returns.

RefreshRequest.title: RefreshRequest
RefreshRequest.description:
Request body for POST /v1/auth/refresh.

The refresh_token is optional — the backend also reads it from an
httpOnly cookie set during the callback flow.

ReviewSessionContentAccessRequest.title: ReviewSessionContentAccessRequest
ReviewSessionContentAccessRequest.description: A final decision; approvals default to eight hours and may use a shorter expiry.

RuleMatch.title: RuleMatch
RuleMatch.description: Provenance of a command-rule decision: which rule fired and how.

ScoreDefinition.title: ScoreDefinition
ScoreDefinition.description:
Definition of a single score dimension. Used in both requests and responses.

The ``name`` is a human-readable label (e.g., "API Key Mishandling").
The ``description`` is a short summary for display.
The ``definition`` holds the full rubric text that gets composed into the grading prompt.

``name`` and ``definition`` are optional for backward compatibility with graders
migrated before structured score definitions were introduced.

can_read_findings.title: Can Read Findings
can_read_findings.description: Whether this caller may read this session's findings.

can_read_content.title: Can Read Content
can_read_content.description: Whether this caller may read this session's content. Scrubbed messages remain unavailable.

agent_platform.title: Agent Platform
agent_platform.description: Reported coding agent. Retained SDK adapter identities can name the agent, including for historical sessions stored as 'other'. Reporting does not change the stored ingestion identity. Clients must tolerate additional platform strings.

sources.title: Sources
sources.description: Distinct canonical ingestion sources among retained session messages, sorted; same values as ``SessionSummary.sources``. Empty for a scrubbed session, whose messages are gone.

ScrubbedSessionDetailResponse.title: ScrubbedSessionDetailResponse
ScrubbedSessionDetailResponse.description: Session detail retaining grades but no trajectory content.

applied_decision.description: Original permission action, independent of grading success.

judged_decision.description: Original policy judgment, including a failure-policy fallback.

enforcement_mode.description: Mode in which the original permission action was recorded.

ScrubbedToolCallListItem.title: ScrubbedToolCallListItem
ScrubbedToolCallListItem.description: A retained verdict whose tool-call evidence has been scrubbed.

SessionAggregatesResponse.title: SessionAggregatesResponse
SessionAggregatesResponse.description:
Aggregate session metrics in one response.

Matching/critical counts and trends are driven by each session's newest
deep-review ``severity`` (the same severity source as the session list),
converted from the requested severity threshold to a score floor. Sessions
awaiting a first review are not counted: this reports reviewed verdicts, so a
growing review backlog shows up as a flat matching count rather than a
speculative one.

SessionAnalyticsSummary.title: SessionAnalyticsSummary
SessionAnalyticsSummary.description:
Summary counts for session aggregates.

``matching_sessions`` is a finding (reviews at or above the selected severity
threshold); ``reviewed_sessions`` and ``pending_sessions`` are the coverage that
finding rests on. Read together they separate "nothing dangerous happened" from
"little has been reviewed yet", which ``matching_sessions / total_sessions``
alone cannot distinguish.

``active_users`` counts distinct known owners of sessions in the window;
