``matching_users`` narrows those owners to sessions that meet the selected
severity threshold. Multiple matching sessions from one person count once,
while sessions without an owner remain in the session counts but cannot
contribute to either user count.

``pending_sessions`` is bounded by the reviewer's rolling lookback, so it counts
only sessions still genuinely queued. That makes it a point-in-time level rather
than a total accumulated over the window, and comparing it across periods is
therefore not meaningful.

SessionAnalyticsTrendPoint.title: SessionAnalyticsTrendPoint
SessionAnalyticsTrendPoint.description:
Bucketed trend counts for aggregate charts.

Both are daily-active session counts (distinct sessions with activity in the
bucket), so ``matching_count`` reads directly as a slice of ``total_count``:
those whose deep-review severity meets the requested threshold.

SessionContentAccessRequestListResponse.title: SessionContentAccessRequestListResponse
SessionContentAccessRequestListResponse.description: A page of the caller's requests, ordered newest first.

SessionContentAccessRequestStatus.title: SessionContentAccessRequestStatus
SessionContentAccessRequestStatus.description: Stored request lifecycle; expiry is derived from the approval's validity window.

SessionContentAccessRequestSummary.title: SessionContentAccessRequestSummary
SessionContentAccessRequestSummary.description:
Request history without session contents or other users' profile details.

An approved request remains approved after ``valid_until``; expiry is derived
from the timestamps rather than stored as a separate review decision.

SessionContentAccessRequestView.title: SessionContentAccessRequestView
SessionContentAccessRequestView.description: Review queues derived from stored decisions and the approval validity window.

SessionDeepReviewResponse.title: SessionDeepReviewResponse
SessionDeepReviewResponse.description:
The deep-review work a session viewer should see on load.

``current`` is an unfinished review if one exists, whoever queued it;
otherwise the latest review of the session's current transcript; otherwise
null, meaning no review was ever requested for it.

SessionDetailResponse.title: SessionDetailResponse
SessionDetailResponse.description: Discriminated available/scrubbed detail response with a stable schema name.

SessionFilterOptionsResponse.title: SessionFilterOptionsResponse
SessionFilterOptionsResponse.description: Available filter options for session list/search responses.

SessionPermissionDecisions.title: SessionPermissionDecisions
SessionPermissionDecisions.description:
Per-session counts of notable Watcher permission decisions.

Each field counts the tool-call decisions in the session that classify into
the corresponding notable category (see ``NotableDecisionCategory``). The
classification matches the Analyzer's transcript view so the session list
and the transcript detail agree on what counts as, e.g., a Watcher
(automated) denial. Fields are zero when no such decision occurred.

start_date.title: Start Date
start_date.description: Include only sessions with activity at or after this datetime. A session's recorded span runs from its first through its latest message, so a session still in progress matches if it has had activity at or after this time.

end_date.title: End Date
end_date.description: Include only sessions that started on or before this datetime.

sources.title: Sources
sources.description: Match any selected canonical ingestion source among retained session messages. Open set of exact source keys, combined with other filters using AND. The source match covers the full session regardless of the date window.

SessionSearchParams.title: SessionSearchParams
SessionSearchParams.description:
Request body for POST /sessions/search.

Supports all filtering, pagination, and sort options.

agent_platform.title: Agent Platform
agent_platform.description: Reported coding agent. Retained SDK adapter identities can name the agent, including for historical sessions stored as 'other'. Reporting does not change the stored ingestion identity. Clients must tolerate additional platform strings.

sources.title: Sources
sources.description: Distinct canonical ingestion sources among retained session messages, sorted. Known values: 'watcher' (Watcher Live upload), 'tailscale-aperture' (Aperture ingestion), and three keys for other hook ingest, including raw pre-tool-use captures, chosen by the session's retained 'other' conversation ID: 'watcher-gateway' (a gateway integration's prefix, such as 'litellm:'), 'watcher-sdk' (a registered SDK agent's prefix, such as 'github-copilot-cli:'), and 'watcher-hook' (any other ID or none). Hook captures marked as Aperture, and legacy captures without a transport marker, are classified as 'tailscale-aperture'; other source keys pass through. Classification is for reporting only: stored message sources are unchanged. Empty for scrubbed sessions or sessions without stored messages. This is not a complete ingestion history.

SessionSummary.title: SessionSummary
SessionSummary.description: Summary of a session for list responses.

SuggestedModel.title: SuggestedModel
SuggestedModel.description: A model the frontend should offer as a recommended choice.

TokenResponse.title: TokenResponse
TokenResponse.description:
Response from POST /v1/auth/callback and /v1/auth/refresh.

The refresh token is only sent as an httpOnly ``Set-Cookie`` (``refresh_token``),
not in this JSON body — browsers avoid exposing it to page JavaScript.
Server-side clients read it from the cookie jar (e.g. httpx ``response.cookies``).

ToolCallContent.title: ToolCallContent
ToolCallContent.description: Content to include in tool call view.

ToolCallDecisionBatchRequest.title: ToolCallDecisionBatchRequest
ToolCallDecisionBatchRequest.description:
Batch upload tool-call decisions after transcript ingest.

Every decision should refer to a tool-use block already present in the
session's messages. Valid decisions are persisted even when other items in
the same batch cannot be resolved.

ToolCallDecisionBatchResponse.title: ToolCallDecisionBatchResponse
ToolCallDecisionBatchResponse.description:
Result of a tool-call decision batch upload.

``synced_tool_use_ids`` identifies decisions accepted by the server.
``failed_tool_use_ids`` and ``failed_tool_call_grade_ids`` identify items
that were not persisted or linked.

decided_by.description: Who settled the call after Watcher handed it on: `person` (a person answered the permission prompt), `agent_review` (the agent's automated approval reviewer answered it, so there is no `human_decision` and `tool_status` holds the outcome) or `interrupt` (the person interrupted the turn before the call was answered, including while Watcher was still reviewing it). Null when the call is unsettled or the sender does not know who answered. Meaningful for escalations; other decisions may carry a value beside Watcher's own verdict.

ToolCallDecisionDetail.title: ToolCallDecisionDetail
ToolCallDecisionDetail.description:
Persisted decision for one ingested tool call.

Grade scores, models, and per-run provenance live in the nested ``grades``
rows. Callers can select a grade by ``run_kind`` and read that row's grade
payload.

decided_by.description: Who settled the call after Watcher handed it on: `person` (a person answered the permission prompt), `agent_review` (the agent's automated approval reviewer answered it, so there is no `human_decision` and `tool_status` holds the outcome) or `interrupt` (the person interrupted the turn before the call was answered, including while Watcher was still reviewing it). Null when the call is unsettled or the sender does not know who answered. Meaningful for escalations; other decisions may carry a value beside Watcher's own verdict.

ToolCallDecisionPayload.title: ToolCallDecisionPayload
ToolCallDecisionPayload.description:
Payload for one tool-call decision.

The caller identifies the tool call by ``tool_use_id``. The server resolves that
ID against already-ingested assistant messages and stores the decision on
the canonical tool-call row.

ToolCallError.title: ToolCallError
ToolCallError.description: Error raised by a tool call.

decided_by.description: Who settled the call after Watcher handed it on: `person` (a person answered the permission prompt), `agent_review` (the agent's automated approval reviewer answered it, so there is no `human_decision` and `tool_status` holds the outcome) or `interrupt` (the person interrupted the turn before the call was answered, including while Watcher was still reviewing it). Null when the call is unsettled or the sender does not know who answered. Meaningful for escalations; other decisions may carry a value beside Watcher's own verdict.

has_result.title: Has Result
has_result.description: Whether this session contains a tool response for this exact tool-use ID.

ToolCallFindingsResponse.title: ToolCallFindingsResponse
ToolCallFindingsResponse.description: Decision and grades with result availability, never raw session content.

ToolCallGradeDetail.title: ToolCallGradeDetail
ToolCallGradeDetail.description:
Persisted tool-call grade attached to a tool-call decision.

The row contains the grader output and the kind of tool-call grading run.
``input_messages`` (the transcript context the grade was run on) is
returned empty by transcript-oriented endpoints such as trajectory detail:
the stored payload is a transcript prefix per tool call, which dwarfs the
rest of the response and is only needed for grade-provenance audits.

ToolCallGradeKind.title: ToolCallGradeKind
ToolCallGradeKind.description: Tool-call grader run types attached to a tool-call decision.

start_date.title: Start Date
start_date.description: Include only tool calls whose message was recorded at or after this time. Calls are dated by their own message rather than by their session's span, so a session running across the boundary contributes only the calls inside it.

end_date.title: End Date
end_date.description: Include only tool calls whose message was recorded at or before this time.

user_id.title: User Id
user_id.description: Restrict results to one user. Callers without sessions:findings:read:any may only name themselves.

tool_names.title: Tool Names
tool_names.description: Tool names to match with OR semantics. Unknown names are valid and match no calls.

severities.title: Severities
severities.description: Score bands to match with OR semantics, plus not_scored for calls with no usable gateway or triage score.

decision_categories.title: Decision Categories
decision_categories.description: Permission outcomes to match with OR semantics. Cleared selects calls Watcher allowed without asking.

ToolCallSearchFilters.title: ToolCallSearchFilters
ToolCallSearchFilters.description: Filter options for the tool-call list. Every field is optional and ANDed.

sort_by.title: Sort By
sort_by.description: Field used to order matching calls.

sort_order.title: Sort Order
sort_order.description: Direction for the primary sort field.

ToolStatus.title: ToolStatus
ToolStatus.description: Final execution status of the tool call.

ToolUseResult.title: ToolUseResult
ToolUseResult.description: Tool use result from Claude Code. Shape varies - accept any fields.

TrajectoryDetailResponse.title: TrajectoryDetailResponse
TrajectoryDetailResponse.description: Full trajectory detail from GET /v1/trajectories/{id} or /sessions/{sid}/trajectories/{tid}.

TrajectorySummary.title: TrajectorySummary
TrajectorySummary.description: Summary of a trajectory for list responses.

TrajectoryView.title: TrajectoryView
TrajectoryView.description:
Content density of a trajectory response.

``truncated`` elides heavy payloads for display: tool outputs and user pastes are
capped with ``content_truncated``/``content_original_chars`` marker fields and
``data`` content blocks are replaced by size stubs. ``extended`` is
storage-faithful. ``truncated`` is the default, so a data consumer (research
export, offline analysis) must explicitly request ``extended`` — omitting the
parameter never ships storage-faithful payloads by accident.

TriageAssessment.title: TriageAssessment
TriageAssessment.description:
A fast triage pass's verdict on the gated call, as data.

The server renders this into the monitor prompt's triage section; senders
never format prompt text. All fields optional — placeholders are the
server's concern.

TriageResult.title: TriageResult
TriageResult.description: The triage monitor's verdict on the gated call.

UpdateGraderRequest.title: UpdateGraderRequest

UpdateMonitorCustomizationRequest.title: UpdateMonitorCustomizationRequest
UpdateMonitorCustomizationRequest.description:
Request body for PUT /v1/monitors/customization.

An empty ``instructions`` string clears the instructions. The server
validates content (length cap, reserved delimiter sequences); the schema
bound here is a coarse mirror of that cap.

UrlCitation.title: UrlCitation
UrlCitation.description: A citation that refers to a URL.

resets_at.title: Resets At
resets_at.description: Midnight UTC on the first of next month, when the caps reset.

calls_used.title: Calls Used
calls_used.description: Error-free non-triage grader calls this period.

UsageLimitsResponse.title: UsageLimitsResponse
UsageLimitsResponse.description:
Current-month grading limit status from GET /v1/usage/limits.

No dollar figures: an org over its dollar cap reports stopped with its call
figures still under the limit.

UserFilter.title: UserFilter
UserFilter.description:
Include or exclude selected owners within the caller's session read scope.

Both fields are required; omit the entire filter to select all permitted
owners. Include matches any listed owner; exclude removes all listed owners
and retains unattributed sessions. Unknown UUIDs match nothing in include
mode and remove nothing in exclude mode. Duplicate IDs are removed while
preserving their first occurrence, including in serialized audit records.
This selection never grants permission to read the selected owners' data.

UserListItem.title: UserListItem
UserListItem.description:
Per-user row exposed in ``GET /v1/users`` list responses.

Includes ``email``: listing requires the ``users:read:any`` permission,
which is also the permission that gates reading other users' emails, so
every caller who can list users may see them.

permissions.title: Permissions
permissions.description: Effective permission slugs for client UI gates: explicit grants plus known Watcher permissions granted by built-in roles. WorkOS widget permissions remain explicit.

role.title: Role
role.description: The caller's role in the active organization, for display only; gating belongs on ``permissions``, which includes built-in role grants. Under WorkOS this is the role the token names; proxy auth reports admin, org-viewer, or member. Null when the authentication in use vouches for no single role.

UserSummary.title: UserSummary
UserSummary.description:
User shape exposed by ``/v1/users/me`` and admin views.

Includes ``email`` since the caller is either looking at themselves
(``/me``) or has admin/cross-user-read permissions.
``workos_user_id`` is not exposed — it's an internal identity-provider
key, not a user-facing identifier.

Verdict.title: Verdict
Verdict.description:
The decision-level view of why a call was decided, whichever stage decided it.

What a caller shows or logs regardless of `decision_source`: the deciding
stage's score banded into a label, and the summary and explanation chosen
for the caller (a rule's label for rule decisions, fixed text for
`grading_error` and `bypass`, the monitor's own text otherwise). The
per-stage models on completed responses (`rule`, `triage`, `gateway`) are
the evidence behind it and are null when that stage did not run. The score
is null when no graded stage decided. Paused and unnamed calls have no
stage results because they skip evaluation.

VersionResponse.title: VersionResponse
VersionResponse.description:
Response from GET /v1/version - the build stamped into this deployment.

The build stamp deliberately excludes a timestamp: it must be a pure
function of the tagged commit so identical release inputs produce
identical, reproducible artifacts.

BearerAuth.description: JWT access token from WorkOS AuthKit sign-in

ApiKeyAuth.name: x-api-key
ApiKeyAuth.description: WorkOS API key (created via Organization → API Keys)
